Three episodes of acute hepatitis with jaundice occurred in a patient taking terfenadine intermittently over a period of 17 months.1 Liver function tests returned to nor- mal after the drug was stopped. Two further cases2 of cholestatic hepatitis associated with terfenadine have been reported. Again, liver function tests returned to normal after drug withdrawal. A study3 by the Boston Collaborative Drug Surveillance Program of 210 683 patients who had received prescriptions for terfena- dine concluded that the use of terfenadine was rarely associated with important idiopathic liver disease. The investigators found only 3 cases of acute liver disease where a causal connection to terfenadine could not be ruled out; all these patients had also re- ceived a hepatotoxic drug and had made a full recovery. 1. Terfenadine and risk of acute liver disease. Br J Clin Pharmacol 1998; 46: 251–3. Effects on the nervous system. Non-sedating effects on the CNS have been reported after a single dose of terfenadine;1 these have included anxiety, palpitations, and insomnia.
